title: Ranking windows: SQL's `rank`, `ntile` spreads the remainder to the first buckets
verdict: SQL ranks, NULLs ranked first ascending; `ntile` front-loads; ties in arrival order
description: `rank`, `dense_rank`, `percent_rank` and `cume_dist` follow SQL: NULL keys are ranked, first in ascending order (two NULLs share rank 1). `row_number` numbers ties in the order the rows arrive, which after a shuffle varies (spark-window-values).
`ntile(n)` gives the first `rows mod n` buckets one row more: 7 rows into 3 buckets are 3, 2, 2; `ntile(10)` over 7 rows numbers them 1 to 7. `ntile(0)` is rejected when the query is analysed.
reference: `rank`, `dense_rank`, `row_number` over the window's order, NULLs placed by the key's direction; `percent_rank`, `cume_dist`, `ntile` as SQL; ties in any order (`tie_order`). Spark is native.

evidence.note: `NTile`: `bucketSize = n / buckets`, the first `n % buckets` buckets one larger

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
